This Appeal Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Aurad-B (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.515/2013, vide judgment and award dated 11.04.2017.
2.

The claimant aged 27 years and an agriculturist met with a motor vehicle accident on 03.02.2013,
when he was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-38/K- 4398, which was dashed against by a medium goods vehicle bearing registration No.MH-26/AD-5276 (henceforth referred as 'offending vehicle').

The claimant suffered injuries on his right leg and was shifted to General Hospital, Aurad and later to General Hospital, Bidar and then to NIMS Hospital, Punjagutta,
Hyderabad where he was treated from 04.02.2013 to 26.02.2013.
He NC: 2023:KHC-K:1244 underwent a surgery for fixing the fracture of femur and tibia but which was unsuccessful and his right leg below the knee was amputated.
The claimant claimed that amputation of the right leg below knee affected his ability to engage in agricultural activities.

He claimed that he was earning Rs.12,000/- per month and due to amputation, he could not engage in any agricultural activity and hence, filed a claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
3. The claim petition was contested by the insurer, who denied the accident as well as negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It however contended that it was the claimant, who was negligent and was responsible for the accident.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P41.
He examined a doctor as PW.2, who deposed that due to the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1244 amputation, the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 75% to the limb.
A representative of the insurer was examined as RW.1 and marked Exs.R1 to R3.
The officer of the Regional Transport Office was examined as RW.2 and driver of the offending vehicle was examined as RW.3.

Prahlad S/O Subhash Rao vs Babu Sab And Anr on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33542501/
2 5.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
It also held that the claimant had suffered fracture of tibia and fibula and shaft of right femur and that his right leg below the knee was amputated.
It considered the evidence of PW.2 and held that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 35% to the whole body.

It considered the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month and awarded the following compensation:
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1244 Towards loss of future Rs.4,28,400/- income Towards medical expenses Rs.3,50,000/- Towards loss of pain and Rs.25,000/-
suffering Towards loss of amenities Rs.15,000/- Towards attendant Charges Rs.5,000/-
Loss of income during Rs.10,000/-
bedridden period Total Rs.8,33,400/-
 6.
The Tribunal directed the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded, the claimant is before this Court.

7. The learned counsel for the appellant/claimant contended that under the provisions of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923, the amputation below knee is a NC: 2023:KHC-K:1244 schedule injury in respect of which disability is assessed at 50% to the whole body.

He submitted that the Tribunal must have assessed the disability suffered by the claimant at 50% having regard to the fact that the claimant was an agriculturist and therefore, the disability suffered by him affected his functions as an agriculturist.
He submitted that assessment of disability under the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 is done scientifically and the same could be applied in the present case also.
He further submitted that the notional income of the claimant must have been considered at a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month as against Rs.6,000/- per month considered by the Tribunal.
He further submitted that the Tribunal failed to award adequate compensation towards loss of amenities, attendant charges and loss of income during period of treatment.
He also contended that the claimant had lost his right foot and therefore, the Tribunal must have awarded compensation for purchasing a prosthetic foot.

Prahlad S/O Subhash Rao vs Babu Sab And Anr on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33542501/
3 8.

Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent/insurer contended that PW.2 deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 75% to the limb and therefore, the Tribunal was justified in assessing the disability at 35%.
He submitted that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the conventional heads is just and proper.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant as well as the learned counsel for the respondent/insurer.
10. The claimant had suffered injuries in the accident involving the offending vehicle.
He was initially treated at General Hospital, Aurad and thereafter shifted to General Hospital, Bidar.
He was then shifted to NIMS Hospital, Punjagutta, Hyderabad, where he underwent a surgery for fixation of fracture of femur and tibia.

He availed further treatment at Kalyani Ortho Centre and Hospital,
Udgir, where his right leg below knee was amputated.

sentences.text: Therefore, he was deprived of his ability of NC: 2023:KHC-K:1244 movement without support.
The Tribunal must have therefore considered the disability suffered by the claimant at 50% as is done in the case of employment related injury under the Employees Compensation Act, 1923.
Therefore, the disability suffered by the claimant had to be considered at 50% to the whole body.
As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant the notional income of the claimant must have been considered at a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month.
The Tribunal must have awarded adequate compensation towards pain and suffering, attendant charges, incidental expenses, travelling expenses etc.
It must have also awarded adequate compensation towards loss of amenities and also for the cost of prosthetic foot.
In that view of the matter, the compensation to which the claimant is entitled to is re
- determined as follows:

NC: 2023:KHC-K:1244 Pain and suffering Rs.40,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.3,50,000/-
Loss of income during the Rs.21,000/-
period of treatment (Rs.7,000x3)
Loss of income due to Rs.7,14,000/-
permanent disability (Rs.7,000x12x17x50%)
Loss of amenities Rs.60,000/-
Attendant charges, Rs.30,000/-
transportation charges and nutritious food Cost of prosthetic limb Rs.1,00,000/-

Prahlad S/O Subhash Rao vs Babu Sab And Anr on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33542501/
4 11.
In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part and the compensation of Rs.8,33,400/- determined by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.13,00,000/-.
The enhanced compensation of Rs.4,66,600/- shall be paid by the insurer to the claimant along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment and award.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period of 3 years.
